title: Merge fallthrough postmortem - quick notes
body:
Context and why I pulled this together:

- Late-night merge into main (PR #4892) introduced a subtle routing fallthrough causing requests to match an older policy when a newer policy was deployed simultaneously. User-facing impact: transient 5-20% increase in tail latency for the affected model route; no data exposure.
- This doc is my personal, messy record: hypotheses, quick repro, short-term mitigations, and ideas for a more durable fix. Not a polished incident report.

What happened (reconstructed):
- Two parallel changes: (A) policy routing cleanup (PR A) to de-duplicate route keys, (B) rollout toggles for model variant selection (PR B). Both touched route selection code in routes/router.go and the policy cache invalidation path.
- Merge order and timing: PR A merged, CI green. PR B merged ~3 minutes later while a small release job was still reconciling cache state in staging and then main.
- Race window: cache invalidation + map re-assignment produced a temporary state where the router matched by fallback ordering rather than explicit key lookup. That produced fallthrough for a subset of requests where the sequence-length heuristic was non-deterministic.

Quick repro notes (dev machine):
- Start local router with small config: ./dev/run-router --config=testdata/fallthrough.yaml
- Apply invalidation in loop: curl -XPOST localhost:8080/invalidate-cache?key=policy
- Hit the route with a seed-based generator to observe mismatch in chosen model variant. Repro frequency ~10% after ~50 invalidations.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Reverted PR B in main (hotfix revert) to stop the rolling interference.
- Force full cache invalidation in prod services and staged restart of router pods behind a canary.
- Short-term: added a synchronous barrier in the invalidation path to avoid concurrent map reassign + read (ugly but effective).

Open hypotheses (ranked):
1) Unsafe map replace pattern: we reassign the route map atomically but readers access nested mutable objects (KV caches) causing read of partially-updated structs.
2) Non-idempotent invalidation handler when multiple calls in-flight leads to transient stale entries with fallback semantics.
3) A subtle change in sequence-length heuristic (PR A) altered ordering of candidate variants, making the fallback path more likely to be chosen under race.

Questions for follow-up:
- Who authored PR A/PR B? (A: @Ethan; B: @Laila) Can they sketch the expected invariants for route map replacement?
- Do we have tests that exercise concurrent invalidation + route lookup at unit/integration level? If not, add a stress test harness.
- Are any other consumers relying on the fallback ordering as a feature? (If yes, we need a compatibility shim.)

Short TODOs (me + immediate):
- [ ] Write a unit test that spawns N invalidations + M readers and asserts determinism (owner: Sofia). Target: 2025-11-14.
- [ ] Replace current map-replace pattern with a copy-on-write immutable snapshot struct for router config (owner: Ethan). Estimate: 3d prototype.
- [ ] Add a canary check that validates route selection invariants before serving traffic (owner: Laila).
- [ ] Add observability: emit a metric when fallback match is chosen and tag with current config hash (owner: Sofia).
- [ ] Postmortem draft for incident tracker (owner: Sofia). Due: 2025-11-12.

Refactor idea sketches (brain dump):
- Snapshot approach: maintain RouterSnapshot { configHash, routes: []RouteSnapshot } where RouteSnapshot contains only immutable primitives and precomputed matchers. Reader swaps pointer to RouterSnapshot atomically. No nested mutation.
- Staged deploy pattern: when rolling out routing changes, publish new RouterSnapshot then wait for consumers to observe the configHash via a light-weight handshake before the change is marked active. Could be implemented as a readiness endpoint queried by sidecars.
- Add a test harness service that fuzzes invalidation ordering and produces a deterministic repro script that can be run in CI. Useful to prevent regressions.

Reviewer checklist (personal):
- Does the PR change any shared in-memory data structure that is read without locking? If yes, flag for co-review with platform memory model.
- Look for map reassigns that hold references to mutable inner objects.
- Check for idempotence on HTTP invalidation endpoints.
- Look for changes to heuristics that affect ordering assumptions (sorting, stable sort, map iteration).
- Confirm metrics telemetry exists for key decision points (route chosen, fallback chosen, config hash).

Rollback plan template (fast):
- Revert PR via revert commit and trigger deploy pipeline.
- If revert fails, patch to force explicit config hash bump + full invalidation + orchestrated pod restart in small batches.

Notes to self (less formal):
- Don't deploy two routing-touching PRs in the same 10-minute window without explicit coordination. Add a small note to the release checklist.
- We need a lightweight gate in the console that warns: "concurrent routing changes detected" when two PRs modify router.go or routes/ files within 30 minutes. Maybe a GH bot that comments.
- My barrier hack worked but is technical debt. Schedule time to implement snapshot approach next sprint.

Linked debugging artifacts (local):
- fallthrough.yaml (small config used to repro) -> stored in local /home/sofia/dev/playground/fallthrough.yaml
- small repro script: ./scripts/fuzz-invalidate.sh
- traces: /var/tmp/repro-traces/2025-11-02-19:42.json

Final loose plan (next 2 weeks):
1) Add deterministic concurrency unit tests + simple CI job (1 week).
2) Implement RouterSnapshot prototype + bench it (1 week).
3) Rollout snapshot-based change behind feature flag and measure fallback metric drop (canary first).
4) Update runbook and release checklist to include coordination note.

End of notes.

-- Sofia

(If anyone stumbles on this doc and wants to riff, add comments or ping me in #eng-serving-runtime.)
